title: How Primitive Will Our Descendants Find Us?
summary: Josh and Chuck close out 2023 with a look at practices future descendants may consider primitive or barbaric. Topics include spanking (US state and school laws, international bans, a 2018 study), chemotherapy and its move toward targeted treatment, antibody drug conjugates, mRNA cancer vaccines, AI-assisted personalized cancer care, organ transplant shortcomings, organ growing and 3D bioprinting, cultured (lab-grown) meat and meat demand, driverless cars and the Cruise incident, drunk driving, GDP as a measure of progress, Peter Singer's circle of concern, and burning fossil fuels and climate-related deaths. Opens with tour announcements and Spotify Wrap listener stats and closes with New Year wishes.
topics: meat demand and greenhouse gas emissions

segments.title: Tour announcements
segments.summary: Hosts announce January 2024 live shows in Seattle, Portland, and San Francisco (Sketchfest) and point to ticket links.
topics: stuff you should know live shows

segments.title: Year-end banter and Spotify Wrap
segments.summary: Hosts discuss listener Spotify Wrap statistics, a listener with very high listening minutes, and listenership in many countries including Mexico.

segments.title: Looking forward at barbaric practices
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode premise: looking back at past habits such as smoking on planes and jello salads, then considering what descendants will judge us for.

segments.title: Spanking
segments.summary: Discussion of a 2018 American Family Survey finding that about half of Americans agree with spanking, declining support across generations, research on spanking and child behavior, a 2018 study of sixty-two countries that banned spanking, and US law allowing school corporal punishment in seventeen states.

segments.title: Transition to chemotherapy
segments.summary: Hosts note chemotherapy has reduced cancer death rates but is indiscriminate, and that future treatment is likely to be more targeted.

segments.title: Targeted cancer treatments and AI
segments.summary: Explanation of antibody drug conjugates that deliver chemo drugs to tumor cells, mRNA-based tumor vaccines, and personalized cancer care using AI to analyze a tumor's genetics, with cost as a barrier.

segments.title: Organ transplants and growing organs
segments.summary: Discussion of transplant rejection rates, organ shortages, and unused donated kidneys. Covers growing skin from stem cells for burn victims, growing organs in the lab, the cloned sheep Dolly, and 3D bioprinting of ears and possibly livers.

segments.title: Meat, lab-grown meat, and animal welfare
segments.summary: Discussion of growing global meat demand, livestock emissions and animal welfare, a bloat-treatment video of cows, predictions that cultured meat could supply much of meat consumption by 2040, a lab-grown Wagyu steak, and a Dutch company making cultured sausage without fetal bovine serum.
topics: meat demand and greenhouse gas emissions

segments.title: Driverless cars and drunk driving
segments.summary: Predictions that ride-hailing will reduce car ownership and that driverless cars are coming, the Cruise setbacks in San Francisco including a pedestrian incident and loss of California permits, driver-assist features, and drunk driving accounting for about thirty percent of traffic fatalities.

segments.title: GDP and circle of concern
segments.summary: Discussion of measuring progress by GDP versus human well-being, economist Kate Raworth's critique, and Peter Singer's idea of an expanding circle of concern.

segments.title: Fossil fuels and climate change deaths
segments.summary: Discussion of future judgment of burning fossil fuels, a University of Wisconsin-Madison estimate of premature deaths and healthcare costs from air pollution, projected climate-related deaths, and a predicted oil market decline this decade.

segments.title: New Year sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts wish listeners a happy new year, thank listeners, and invite email contact; the episode closes with the production credit.
